title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-taylor-wip
content:
Goals:
- Capture breadcrumbs for last 72h incident where traces and metrics dropped for routing-service in us-west-2.
- Record commands tried, quick hypotheses, and next steps for follow-up.

Timeline / symptoms:
- 2025-02-11 02:14 UTC: Alert firing: `routing-service:trace-drop-high` (80% traces missing for 30m).
- Same window: prometheus scrape errors for `routing-service` (scrape failures ~75% from node-exporter targets).
- Logs show repeated 403s from prom scrapers to metrics endpoint (~02:10-02:45 UTC).
- OTEL spans from routing-service stopped being exported to collector between 02:05-02:20 then resumed.

What I checked (commands + outputs):
1) k8s pods & events (us-west-2 cluster):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=routing-service -o wide
  -> pods restarted around 02:03-02:08 (OOMKilled on one node, others healthy)
- kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=otel-collector -o wide
  -> collectors in us-west-2 had 1 pod in CrashLoopBackOff for ~10m (check logs below)

2) otel collector logs (collector-0):
- kubectl -n observability logs otel-collector-0
  -> ERROR: failed to authenticate to storage backend: token expired (stack trace snippet).
  -> Followed by `panic: unable to reinitialize exporter` and restart.

3) prometheus scrape errors (from prometheus-operator logs):
- curl -sS http://prometheus-usw2:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.health=="down")'
  -> target: routing-service:9100, lastError: "403 Forbidden: service account token invalid"

4) kube-apiserver / kube-controller-manager events on affected node:
- kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<node-xyz>
  -> tokens for kubelet rotation failing (kubelet unable to refresh from kube-controller-manager) — nodes showed short TTL mismatch.

5) log ingestion (vector/td-agent)
- vector logs showed backoff connecting to kafka: `ERROR: 503 Service Unavailable` during 02:00-02:20
- local buffer files present (~150MB) on node, ingestion resumed after collectors restarted.

Error snippets: 
- OTEL: "failed to authenticate to storage backend: token expired"
- Prom: "403 Forbidden: service account token invalid"
- Vector: "kafka: broker not available (503)"
- App-level: `WARN: span export failed: upstream unreachable`

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Credential rotation gone wrong: a short-lived service account token refresh failed across multiple components (otel collector, prometheus scrape, kubelet), causing simultaneous telemetry drop. Evidence: repeated token-related errors, timing aligned.
2) Control plane incident: kube-controller-manager had transient inability to serve token rotations causing downstream authentication failures. Evidence: node events show rotation issues.
3) Network partition to backend auth/KMS causing token validation failures (less likely because we saw "token expired" explicitly).
4) Rate-limited Kafka cluster leading to log backlog and vector backoff; secondary contributor rather than root cause.

What I tried / mitigation steps (and immediate outcomes):
- Manually rotated the short-lived service account token for otel-collector and restarted pod (kubectl -n observability delete pod otel-collector-0). Outcome: collector resumed exports within ~90s; traces backfilled partially.
- Recreated Prometheus scrape config secret (kubectl -n monitoring delete secret prom-scrape-credentials; kubectl apply -f prom-secret.yaml). Outcome: scrapes recovered, 403s stopped.
- Scaled vector daemonset down/up to flush and re-establish Kafka producers. Outcome: backpressure cleared, buffered files shipped over next ~10m.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did token rotation fail? Check kube-controller-manager logs around 01:55-02:10 UTC (ticketed OBS-5123).
- Did KMS have any maintenance or auth outage? Ask infra/security for KMS audit around timeframe.
- Verify if automation (terraform/apply) triggered token/secret update accidentally (search CI pipelines run history 01:30-02:30).
- Add better instrumentation: alert for successive `service account token invalid` errors across infra components.
- Consider short-term: add a cached fallback token for critical telemetry components to avoid full drop on rotation failure.

Repro steps to validate fix in staging:
1) force rotate service account token in staging (simulate expiry path).
2) observe collector, prometheus behavior; confirm graceful rotation without 5m downtime.
3) induce kafka transient (slow broker) and confirm vector backpressure handling and disk buffering works.

Notes / random crumbs:
- Slack thread: #observability incident-2025-02-11 (see messages from @Priya and @Eli about collector crash).
- GitHub PR that touched prometheus scrape secret handling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/428 (opened 2025-02-09).
- Related Confluence playbook: observability/pipeline-ingestion-playbook (outlines token rotation steps).

Next actions (assignments):
- @Priya: pull kube-controller-manager logs + attach relevant segments to OBS-5123 (due 2025-02-15).
- @Eli: follow up with infra/security on KMS/auth logs (due 2025-02-15).
- @Taylor: implement quick alert for repeated `token invalid` across services and draft mitigation using cached fallback token (due 2025-02-18).

Short-term workaround we applied: created a temporary long-lived token for otel-collector with restricted scope and configured collector to use it until root cause confirmed. NOTE: security aware — this is temporary and will be rotated once fix in place.

End of notes.
